notes: Iteration 2 assertions measure the new goal (architecture and performance first): estimates with numbers, sized waste, a target shape, and ordering. The two seeded/medium baselines are the unchanged iteration-1 runs re-graded against these assertions.

Discriminating assertions: the minimum-versus-actual estimate, ordering of architecture/performance before correctness, and quantified performance findings. Most defect-identification assertions pass for both configurations.

Correctness trade-off: in the tokenizer case the baseline found two real defects the skill run missed (the rejected '\'' escape and the missing `view` keyword); in the seeded case only the baseline caught the CompilerSources.txt build break. The skill run reported 'no tokenizer bugs', which was false. After this run the skill was edited to compare duplicated kind tables directly and to keep recording bugs found while tracing.
Unique skill-run findings: the parser budget integer overflow, the three indistinguishable bracket contexts, the explicit hot/cold verdict and a full target shape for the tokenizer.
Cost: about 11% more tokens and 17% more time than the baseline on average; one run each, so variance is not established.
